title: Powered land for sale: data center, AI and bitcoin mining sites available now (November 2026)
description: Nineteen powered sites available through Invariant in November 2026, from a 1.5 GW Arizona AI campus to energized 2 MW mining sites, with MW, acreage, timing and price.
intro: Invariant has 19 powered sites available as of November 2026, ranging from a 1.5 GW AI campus in Arizona down to energized 2 MW mining sites in Kentucky. Eleven are in the 18 MW to 1.5 GW range that AI, HPC and hyperscale buyers ask for, and most can take load today. Each site below has its own page with the full specification, power path and the documents we check before an introduction.
takeaways: Large campuses: Arizona 1.5 GW, Nevada 375 MW, Ohio 300 MW, Indianapolis 200 MW, Wisconsin 150 MW.
Energized today: North Carolina 18 MW on 207 acres, Kentucky 30 MW, Texas 44 MW, Oklahoma City 55 MW contracted.
Small and fast: turnkey mining and edge sites from $500k to $1.7M in Kentucky, Oklahoma, Texas and Iowa.
International: a 20 MW-ready Finnish site with district heat offtake.
Tell us your MW, state and energize-by date. We send matching sites, including ones not listed here.

sections.heading: Every site available right now

rows: 200 MW, load study done, AEP I&M
45 MW live BTM gas, to 250 MW
10 MW, upgradeable to 20 MW, heat offtake
2.25 MW AI edge at a power plant

sections.heading: Large campuses for AI and hyperscale (150 MW and up)

blocks.text: Five sites clear 150 MW. Arizona is the outlier: 1.5 GW studied by APS, a 2x345 kV switchyard on the land and more than 15,000 acres. Nevada (375 MW) and Ohio (300 MW) both target 2027 energization on transmission voltage. Indianapolis has something most 200 MW pitches lack, a completed utility load study. Wisconsin is the fastest of the group, with its 150 MW substation already built and 80 MW available now.
Kansas belongs here too, though it is a different animal: 45 MW of behind-the-meter gas generation running from owned wells, with a path to 250 MW.

sections.heading: Energized sites for neocloud and inference (18 MW to 55 MW)

blocks.text: If your problem is 2026 and 2027 capacity, start with these. North Carolina has 18 MW live with 17 months of bills at 6.2 cents all-in. Pikeville, Kentucky has 30 MW on AEP Kentucky Power and finished rezoning. The Texas metro property has 44 MW and a million square feet of buildings. Oklahoma City has 55 MW under two executed OG&E agreements.

sections.heading: Turnkey mining and edge sites (under 6 MW)

blocks.text: Six smaller sites are selling with transformers, containers and utility accounts in place: four in Kentucky, one in Oklahoma, one in Houston. Plus a 2.25 MW AI edge site inside the fence of a municipal power plant in Muscatine, Iowa. Prices run from $500,000 to $1.7 million, and most can close in weeks.

sections.heading: How Invariant works with buyers

blocks.text: We start from power evidence, not land. For each site, we check the utility paperwork (studies, service agreements, will-serve letters), the zoning status and the title before we introduce a buyer. Specifications on these pages are as marketed by the seller. We confirm them against documents during diligence, and we tell you which ones we could not confirm.
Need something that is not on this list? Send us the MW, the state, the acreage and the date you need power. Most of what we place is never posted publicly.

faqs.question: Where can I find powered land for a data center in the US?
faqs.answer: Invariant has 19 powered sites available as of November 2026, including Arizona (1.5 GW), Nevada (375 MW), Ohio (300 MW), Indianapolis (200 MW), Wisconsin (150 MW) and North Carolina (18 MW live). Book a call or text (628) 220-8972 for details.

faqs.answer: North Carolina (18 MW), Kentucky near Pikeville (30 MW), a Texas metro property (44 MW), Oklahoma City (55 MW contracted), Wisconsin (80 MW from a built substation), plus smaller turnkey sites in Kentucky, Oklahoma, Texas and Iowa.

faqs.question: What is the largest site available?
faqs.answer: The Arizona AI campus: 1.5 GW of APS-studied Phase 1 capacity on more than 15,000 acres, with 4.5 GW more filed.

faqs.answer: Yes. The sites on this page are a subset. Tell us your requirements on a call and we will share others that fit.

faqs.question: How do you verify a powered site?
faqs.answer: We check the utility documents first (load study, service agreement or will-serve letter), then zoning and title, before introducing a buyer. We flag anything we could not confirm.

title: Arizona powered land for sale: 1.5 GW AI campus with APS grid power and a PPA
description: A 15,000+ acre Arizona AI campus with 1.5 GW of APS-studied grid capacity, an onsite 2x345 kV switchyard, I-40 and BNSF access, available to buy or lease.
intro: This is a 1.5 GW powered land campus in Arizona, available now through Invariant to buy or lease. Phase 1 capacity has been studied by Arizona Public Service (APS), a further 4.5 GW is filed, and an existing 2x345 kV switchyard on the property can carry roughly the first 200 MW. Grid power is scheduled for 2027, with onsite generation available in under a year. The land position is over 15,000 acres, with more than 5,000 acres already zoned for data centers.
takeaways: 1.5 GW Phase 1 studied by APS, 4.5 GW more in the queue, power sleeved through APS under a PPA.
Existing 2x345 kV switchyard onsite for the first ~200 MW, with a 500 kV-ready loop.
15,000+ acres secured (expandable past 30,000), 5,000+ acres zoned for data centers, about 1 acre per MW.
Direct I-40 and BNSF rail access, Tier-1 fiber on site, Qualified Opportunity Zone and DOE energy community.
Price on request under NDA. Book a call for the data room.

sections.heading: The site at a glance

rows: 1.5 GW Phase 1 studied by APS; 4.5 GW more filed
Existing 2x345 kV switchyard (first ~200 MW); 500 kV-ready loop
Grid power 2027; onsite power in under 12 months
Behind-the-meter generation plus BESS and APS grid on one shared POI, up to 99.99% (N+2)
Two pipelines serving ~200 MW today; 2.7 bcf/d load letter on new 42 inch lines for 2029
15,000+ acres secured, 5,000+ acres zoned for data centers
About 3 months under a special development agreement
I-40 and BNSF rail; outside city limits, no noise restrictions
Buy or lease, powered land plus PPA sleeved through APS

sections.heading: How the power gets to the fence

blocks.text: The structure matters more than the headline number. Generation and the APS grid connect at the same onsite point of interconnection, and APS meters the tenants. According to the seller, APS has confirmed that load can be served early where generation connects at the data center switchyard. In plain terms: a buyer can start on onsite power and roll onto grid supply as the Phase 1 switchyard is built by an APS-certified EPC contractor.

The surrounding hub has about 9.5 GW in the interconnection queue, with roughly 1,500 MW of solar and 500 MW of wind under construction and APS adding 380 MW of gas. That depth is the reason a campus this size is even plausible in one place.

Gas is the second leg. Two existing pipelines can serve about 200 MW now. A load letter for 2.7 bcf/d on new 42 inch lines, targeted for 2029, would in theory support more than 12 GW of gas-fired generation. Treat that as a 2029 option, not a 2027 fact.

sections.heading: Land, zoning and incentives

blocks.text: More than 15,000 acres are under control, with a path past 30,000. Over 5,000 acres are already zoned for data center use, and the seller quotes roughly three months for permitting under a special development agreement. The rule of thumb on this campus is one acre per MW.
The site sits in a Qualified Opportunity Zone, a USDA-eligible area and a DOE-designated energy community. Each of these can change the after-tax math for a buyer, so they belong in the model early.

sections.heading: Who this campus fits

blocks.text: Hyperscale and neocloud buyers that need hundreds of MW on one campus, plus developers who want to phase a multi-GW build on land that is already zoned. It is too big for a 20 MW colocation play. If you need 50 MW, ask us for the smaller Arizona and Southwest sites instead.

sections.heading: What we check before an introduction

items: The APS study documents for Phase 1, including the study date and any conditions or network upgrades.
The PPA term sheet and the sleeving mechanics through APS.
Title and zoning records for the 5,000+ zoned acres, and the special development agreement itself.
Water rights and well permits, which matter more in Arizona than almost anywhere else.
The gas load letter and pipeline in-service dates.

faqs.question: Is this Arizona site available to buy or lease?
faqs.answer: Both. The seller offers the powered land and a PPA sleeved through APS on a buy or lease basis. Pricing is shared under NDA after a call.

faqs.question: How much power is available and when?
faqs.answer: Phase 1 is 1.5 GW of grid capacity studied by APS, with grid power targeted for 2027. Onsite generation can be energized in under a year. A further 4.5 GW has been filed.

faqs.question: What interconnection is already built?
faqs.answer: An existing 2x345 kV switchyard on the property can serve roughly the first 200 MW, and the design includes a 500 kV-ready loop for later phases.

faqs.question: How do I get the data room?
faqs.answer: Book a call with Invariant using the link at the top of this page, or call or text (628) 220-8972. We confirm fit, then arrange the NDA and the data room.

title: North Carolina AI campus for sale: 18 MW live on 207 acres, expandable past 100 MW
description: An energized North Carolina campus with 18 MW live, 12 MW more committed for 2028, a 21 MVA onsite substation, 207 acres, Phase I complete, for $14M.
intro: This North Carolina campus is for sale at $14.0 million with 18 MW already live and billed on two utility services. A further 12 MW is committed for 2028 under a utility Letter of Authorization, and the campus has a path past 100 MW. It sits on a 207-acre core tract in a Tier 1 county with no county zoning, a 21 MVA onsite substation and carrier fiber on the property. All-in power has averaged 6.2 cents per kWh across 17 reconciled billing cycles.
takeaways: 18 MW live today, +12 MW committed for 2028, 100+ MW campus potential.
6.2 cents/kWh all-in over 17 billing cycles and 95 GWh, energy-only 4.2 cents.
207-acre core campus, about 182 acres unconstrained, no county zoning, rail on the boundary.
Diligence done: Phase I with no RECs, geotech, flood model, USACE wetlands determination, USFWS and SHPO concurrence.
$14.0M at closing, with new capacity priced as it energizes.

sections.heading: The site at a glance

rows: 18 MW on two utility services (12 MW + 6 MW)
+12 MW for 2028 under a utility Letter of Authorization
100+ MW, plus a 50+ MW onsite gas generation pathway (~18 months)
6.2 cents/kWh all-in (incl. 7% sales tax, net of DR credits); energy-only 4.2 cents
21 MVA installed (7x 3,000 kVA, 12.47 kV to 415 V)
Carrier fiber on property, up to 100G dual, two more carriers approved
16 racks live at 20 kW each; 60 kW/rack container incoming
207-acre core campus, ~182 acres unconstrained, ~197 more acres at fair market value
Municipal water up to 8 MGD treatment, 4.95 MGD wastewater

sections.heading: Power you can audit, not just a promise

blocks.text: Most powered land pitches stop at a capacity number. This one comes with billing history. The 6.2 cent all-in figure is reconciled across 17 billing cycles and about 95 GWh of consumption, including North Carolina sales tax and net of demand response credits. Monthly cost has ranged from 5.7 to 7.3 cents.

That record is worth a lot in diligence. It tells a lender what the site actually costs to run, and it tells a GPU tenant that the load has been served. The 12 MW committed for 2028 sits under a utility Letter of Authorization. We would still ask for the letter itself before an LOI.

sections.heading: How the expansion is priced

blocks.text: The $14.0M closing price covers the land, the 18 MW live and the existing infrastructure. New capacity is priced as it energizes: $500,000 per MW in 2028, stepping down to a $200,000 per MW floor by 2032. A land lease-back keeps the current load paying while the buyer builds.

Is that cheap? For 18 MW energized today, with zoning not required at the county level and Phase I clean, a buyer is paying under $800,000 per live MW including land. Compare that with greenfield sites still waiting on a load study.

sections.heading: Who this campus fits

blocks.text: AI inference and neocloud operators who need 10 to 30 MW now and a credible route to 100 MW. Also miners converting to HPC who want the substation and fiber already in place. It does not suit a buyer who needs 300 MW on day one.

sections.heading: What we check before an introduction

items: The two utility service agreements and the 2028 Letter of Authorization.
The 17 months of bills that support the 6.2 cent figure.
The Phase I report, wetlands determination and agency concurrence letters.
Title for the core tract and the option terms on the extra ~197 acres.

faqs.question: How much power is live at the North Carolina campus?
faqs.answer: 18 MW is live and billed today on two utility services (12 MW and 6 MW). Another 12 MW is committed for 2028.

faqs.question: What does the power cost?
faqs.answer: About 6.2 cents per kWh all-in across 17 reconciled billing cycles, including 7% state sales tax and net of demand response credits. Energy-only cost is about 4.2 cents.

faqs.question: What is the asking price?
faqs.answer: $14.0 million at closing, including the 18 MW live. Additional capacity is priced as it energizes, from $500,000 per MW in 2028 down to $200,000 per MW by 2032.

faqs.question: Is the site zoned for a data center?
faqs.answer: The county has no zoning, so there is no county rezoning step. The seller has completed a Phase I with no RECs, geotech, a flood model and a USACE wetlands determination.

title: Oklahoma City powered land: 55 MW contracted with OG&E on an 84-acre brownfield

intro: This 84-acre brownfield in Oklahoma City holds 55 MW under two executed OG&E service agreements (15 MW and 40 MW), fed from OG&E's Discovery Substation. It is zoned I-2, has a prior City-approved data center pod permit and a full civil and electrical design set, and carries a 40/44.8 MVA transformer on site. The asking price was $32 million as an asset sale, with a lease-to-own option. Availability moves fast on this one, so confirm status on a call.

Modelled tariff 4.8 cents/kWh, 3.5 to 3.7 cents net after SPP curtailment credits.
I-2 zoning, prior City data center permit, full design set, 40/44.8 MVA transformer on site.
HV feeders to ~36 MW quoted at $1.95M and 90 to 120 working days.

blocks.text: Plenty of Oklahoma land sits near transmission. Far less of it has executed service agreements. Here, the utility paperwork is already signed, the load has run at about 20 MW, and the feeder upgrade to roughly 36 MW has a quote: $1.95 million and 90 to 120 working days.

Oklahoma also exempts electricity and mining equipment from sales tax through 2029 for miners operating under a load-reduction agreement. That helps a bitcoin buyer more than an AI tenant, but it shows up in either model.

sections.heading: Who this site fits

blocks.text: Miners who want to self-mine or host at 3.5 cent power, and HPC developers who want a phased AI build on land that already carries a data center permit. The prior mining operation has been decommissioned, so a buyer starts clean.

The prior data center pod permit and whether it is still valid.

Environmental history of the brownfield parcel.

blocks.text: This is an entity acquisition, which keeps the Kentucky Utilities account, the active demand response contract and the permits in place. blocks.text: Of the four, this is the one with room to grow. It has 5 MW on the PJM grid today (3 MW turnkey, 2 MW more with transformer upgrades) and the land comes with the sale. sections.heading: The site at a glance
Why Ohio keeps showing up on hyperscale shortlists

blocks.text: Ohio sits inside PJM, the largest wholesale market in the US, and has become one of the busiest data center states outside Virginia. The hard part there is no longer land. It is getting a utility to commit capacity on a date. A site with 300 MW already approved and a 2027 date skips the longest step.
Gas at 10,000+ Dth per day also gives a buyer a bridge-power option if the grid date slips. Roughly, that supports on the order of 50 MW of gas-fired generation running around the clock.
